summary.intent: Land the remaining Callisto work by opening and stacking the PR C stack (#217/#218/#220), then launch and complete Wave 1 (W10 declaration tracking, W9a resolver-divergence repro, W9b pre-state alias conflict error), with the orchestrator doing the commits, gating and PRs.
summary.outcome: Stack #217/#218/#220 was opened and linked, and #213/#214/#216 were confirmed merged. Wave 1 ran with only W9a succeeding. The W9b agent's partial work was taken over, verified, gated (`just ci` exit=0) and committed in two commits, while W10's partial work was read but not yet gated, reviewed or committed.

repo: `just ci` is the full gate and runs serially, one branch tip at a time. Each stacked PR must pass it on its own tip.
Agents can't run git or `just ci`, so they leave changes uncommitted and the orchestrator branches from `main`, commits, gates, opens PRs and links them with `gh stack`.
A failing-test-first commit would fail CI at that commit, so a lane's tests go in the same commit as the fix unless they pass without it (characterization tests).
Commit message rules: explain the why, no session links, no history words, one line per paragraph. Changesets are created per PR from the agents' suggested sentences.
Public API changes are checked with `just check-api`. W10 adds a `locator` field on `DependencyEntry` and `DepEdge`, and a new parameter on the `Manifest` trait's `update_dependency_spec`.
New error codes are allocated as the next free code in `docs/errors.md`. W9b's pre-state alias conflict became E305.
The attestation CI job ran green on `main` with `contents: read`, so `attestations: read` is not needed.
The redactor credential lists are separate on purpose. `CALLISTO_PUBLISH_NPM_CONFIG` is a file path, not a secret.

`status` and `version` resolve selectors differently, and this causes six real divergences. `status` uses `PackageId::resolve_unique` (status.rs:46 and :200) and `version` uses `IdentityIndex::resolve_id` via `resolve_target_package` (aggregate.rs:317).
`status --check` exits 1 for a name in no package, while `version` only warns. This is by design per `docs/specs/cli.json`, not a resolver bug.

code.finding: `status` resolves changeset entries with `PackageId::resolve_unique` (lines 46 and 200). That wildcard-matches qualified selectors for ecosystems lacking the name and rejects secondary native names.

`resolve_target_package` calls `IdentityIndex::resolve_id`, an exact lookup on (ecosystem, native name). It accepts secondary native names and ignores qualified selectors for ecosystems lacking the name.
Code comments flag the `matches()` wildcard as a known hazard behind the status/version divergence.
`Workspace` exposes `ws.identity: IdentityIndex`, so `status` could use the version resolver with a small change (not made).

friction: The W10 and W9b implement agents died on ECONNRESET after about 50 minutes, retried once, and failed again, so the review stage never ran.
The agents lack git and `just ci`, so the orchestrator has to do all branching, gating and committing by hand.
The workflow result was truncated, so the full detail lives in the output file and journal.
Comparing agent worktrees against the base needed a custom diff script because git couldn't be used inside them.
